entries.postTitle: How to Tell When Something Is Not for You Anymore

captions.threads:
1/4 there's a specific tired that sleep doesn't fix. you do the thing. you do it well. people tell you you're lucky. and somehow that makes it worse, not better. because now you can't even complain about it without feeling ungrateful.

2/4 the trap is thinking this means you're broken. that gratitude should override the hollow feeling. that if you just optimized harder, hustled smarter, found the right angle, suddenly the misalignment would click into place. it won't. optimization can't fix something that was never meant for you.

3/4 what nobody tells you: the competence can coexist with the wrongness. you can be genuinely skilled at something and have it still drain your life force. your success at it doesn't make it your thing. sometimes it makes it worse because the friction is invisible to everyone but you.

4/4 the realization isn't that you need to quit everything tomorrow. it's that staying should feel like a choice, not a sentence. if it's costing you more than it's giving, if the tired has become the baseline, if you're building someone else's dream while yours collects dust, that's not laziness talking. that's your system telling you something. https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/how-to-tell-when-something-is-not-for-you-anymore
